messages:
deploy-bot: Deployment started: canary rollout v2.14 -> canary set A (10% traffic) at 2026-03-15T15:00:00Z
deploy-bot: Canary health check failing: 3/3 requests 500 in last 30s for /generate endpoint :rotating_light:
inc-bot: @maria (oncall) paging: PagerDuty alert PD-9221 triggered: canary_error_rate_high (severity: high)
maria (oncall): on it, picking this up. @alex (sre) do you have visibility into infra?
alex (sre): looking now, seeing elevated 5xx from canaries. CPU on the canary hosts is fine, but qps spiked unexpectedly.
jin (eng): i just watched the rollout logs — the new ranking feature flag was ramped to 100% inside the canary config by mistake (`ff:new-ranking=true`). that should have stayed off for canary.
maria (oncall): ok hold — is this customer impacting or only internal traffic?
support-bot: multiple customer 500 reports coming in via support queue (ticket #4871, #4872). customers hitting /generate got 500s.
sara (product): that’s bad. which cohort is affected? are paid customers seeing this?
jin (eng): looks like canary routing included some production traffic. feature flag caused a nil deref in ranking code when inputs matched a new edge case.
alex (sre): need to stop traffic to canary, and rollback the flag. can we flip the flag kill-switch?
jin (eng): doing rapid kill: running: ```curl -X POST -H 'Authorization: Bearer REDACT' https://flags.internal/api/v1/flags/new-ranking -d '{"enabled":false}'```
jin (eng): killed flag -> `200 OK`
maria (oncall): flipping canary routing to 0% via deploy control plane now (`/deploys/canary/shutdown`). executing...
deploy-bot: Canary traffic scaled to 0% for set A. ongoing health checks greenening.
alex (sre): starting rollback of v2.14 -> v2.13 on canary. executing `kubectl set image` for canary svc.
inc-bot: Incident status: mitigation in progress. page cleared? updated PD status to acknowledged.
support-bot: updating customer tickets: temporary workaround applied, apologizing and telling them we’re rolling back.
priya (devex): quick note — observability for canary was weaker: the canary-dashboard doesn’t surface the new-ranking error metric and alert thresholds were too permissive (alert fired only after 5m avg). we only had generic 5xx alerts, not the specific ranking_error metric.
maria (oncall): that explains the delayed detection. alerts were noisy and not specific -> SLO burn ambiguity. we need clearer per-feature metrics on canaries.
sara (product): need impact assessment: how many requests failed and for how long? can we quantify SLO burn?
alex (sre): pulling from logs -> approx 2.4k failed requests in the 7-minute window, 95th latency spike to 3.2s before failures. sending numbers to thread.
jin (eng): root cause: feature flag default/validation missing for an optional field; when unusual payload came in ranking path attempted `items[0].score` on empty list. adding guard.
maria (oncall): rollback complete on canary at 15:07Z. no further 5xx observed after 15:09Z. last failure seen timestamp 15:08Z.
inc-bot: Incident status: mitigated -> monitoring. PD incident remains open for postmortem.
priya (devex): follow-ups I propose: 1) add ranking_error metric + dedicated canary dashboard, 2) lower alert window to 1m for canary 5xx, 3) add feature-flag gating checklist during deploys.
sara (product): +1. also require that any feature flag that touches ranking has validation tests and a canary-only safety net.
alex (sre): creating tickets: INF-201 (dashboard), INF-202 (alert tuning), INF-203 (deploy checklist). assigning owners.
maria (oncall): handing off to alex for the postmortem. I’m offshift at 15:30Z, please update PD and close when postmortem is posted.
alex (sre): wilco. will run RCA and include customer impact, timeline, and remediation steps.
jin (eng): sorry team — my bad on the ramp. will follow up with code fix and tests.
support-bot: customers notified of resolution and given credit. closing tickets after confirmation.
inc-bot: Incident timeline note appended.
maria (oncall): thanks all. going offline. :white_check_mark:
